summary:
# NOTES: *Betty Wales, Sophomore* by Margaret Warde (Edith Kellogg Dunton), 1905. Single book; no separate volumes.

## Front matter / Introduction
- Series: Betty Wales Freshman, Junior, Senior, B.A. Illustrator Eva M. Nagel.
- Freshman year at Mrs. Chapin's: nine girls. Katherine Kittredge ("of Kankakee," flighty); Rachel Morrison (steady, strongest); Roberta Lewis (shy, pairs with Mary Brooks); Mary Brooks (sophomore, pranks, practical jokes, put Betty's picture in grind book, Mountain Day secret, "rumor" story); Helen Adams (Betty's roommate, forlorn, awkward, studious; later Helen Chase Adams); Betty Wales (fun, easygoing).
- Eleanor Watson: snobbish, beautiful; helped in Freshman book by Dorothy King and Miss Ferris (faculty).
- Harding College; Mrs. Chapin's; Belden House; Hilton House; Westcott House; Winsted College nearby (Paul West).

## Ch I MOVING IN
- Betty at Belden House, room with green lizard (ornament), Japanese screen, green vase (Madeline says belongs on bookcase).
- Eleanor returns, softened; father Judge Watson, brother Jim (Cornell). Rachel at small white house off campus; Katherine at Westcott; Eleanor at Hilton.
- Madeline Ayres (tall, stately, from "Bohemia, New York," Washington Square studio; father painter, mother mends tapestries; villa near Sorrento; speaks French, German, Spanish, Italian, Bengali; class secretary). Visits Betty's room, helps unpack.
- Nita Reese (single room fourth floor). Babe, Bob, Babbie (the B's, from Westcott) spend night; Bob's father's five-pound chocolate box.
- Emily Davis (Betty's swimming friend).

## Ch II ELEANOR'S FRESHMAN
- Sophomore reception. Polly Eastman (Jean's freshman cousin) ill; Eleanor's violets. Betty asks Eleanor to take Madeline; Eleanor instead invites Dora Carlson (from Ohio farm, father, Market Street No. 50; keeps house for father since twelve). Eleanor gives her a dance, violets.
- Jean Eastman (Hill girl, scornful). Paul West (Winsted). Eleanor: "Good times don't have to last." Invites Dora to Hilton Sunday dinner.
- Katherine mocks "crush." Eleanor: "Dora is frank... ought to have been a man."

## Ch III PARADES AND PARTIES
- Madeline elected class secretary; Miss Felton (Spanish), Miss Raymond (theme class); Henry Ward Beecher handwriting joke. Madeline dislikes Eleanor's wire-pulling.
- Helen takes up gym, persuaded by Madeline; Betty cuts her gym suit neck. Helen aims for literary honors.
- Republican parade (Mary Brooks, Madeline, Nita defeated candidate in chains, Roosevelt/Fairbanks). Roberta laughs, stays.
- Hallowe'en parties (Belden masquerade; Hilton country; Westcott spook party).
- Mary hints about societies; Helen overhears senior that Betty will be taken in.

## Ch IV ELEANOR WATSON, AUTHORESS
- Eleanor's struggle to "go round." Writes theme (story about man and girl); Alice Waite; Christy Mason plans construction car ride.
- Eleanor sits on stairs, theme box; freshman Christy noted; Eleanor deposits theme (late/at 4pm box for Themes L to Z). Ride; guitar. Jean says Miss Raymond entertaining Prof. Morris.
- Eleanor wants theme back; Miss Raymond reads story to class ("extraordinary work"). Eleanor tries to reclaim it; says "It ought never to have gone in." Dorothy King (business manager, Argus) asks for story; Eleanor reluctantly gives it. Dorothy angry, later apologizes.

## Ch V POINTS OF VIEW
- Harding Aid Society (loans, Loan Fund $10,000 before Christmas). Mary Brooks runs "Show"; Madeline supplies costumes (mustache, Persian silk, turban). Marion Lawrence (Loan Fund chairman), Marion Lustig.
- Show: fortune-tellers, circus, menagerie (white baby elephant, Happy Family: red lion seniors, purple cow juniors, green dragon sophomores, yellow chicken freshmen; "Animal Song"), Mlle. Zita, Emily Davis as circus manager/ticket. Madeline's play "The Animal Fair." Raised $50 for Aid.
- Madeline on Eleanor: "She's anxious... I'm sorry for her." Eleanor palm reading.

## Ch VI ON AMBITION
- Walk with Miss Hale (Ethel, Nan's friend; formerly snubbed Nan; had to be taught by Nan). Miss Hale doubts Eleanor.
- Nan and Will Wales arrive (telegram "Meet the 7:10 to-night. WILL"); stay a week; Mary takes Will to gym gallery; Will and John Parsons; sleighing at Winsted.
- Betty invites Eleanor to dinner with Will at Cuyler's; Eleanor refuses (Beatrice Egerton, senior). Helen and Betty argue about ambition.

## Ch VII ON TO MIDYEARS
- Betty and Roberta go to Cleveland for Christmas (Mr. Wales; smallest sister; Will). Roberta unhappy, wants to leave; Betty advises Jabberwock party.
- Rachel's room tea: Katherine says she's dropping Eleanor ("lady Eleanor"); saw her with Beatrice at Cuyler's. Betty defends Eleanor, Dora Carlson. Eleanor to Betty: "this fall I forgot who I was... Now I've come to my senses."

## Ch VIII THE "FIRST FOUR"
- Nita's birthday spread (Feb 9). Bob's bet re: Dramatic Club. Babe's pretend French maid, rents riding horse. Society elections: Dramatic Club first (first four), Clio second. Bob elected (war-whoop); Eleanor elected (Beatrice Egerton pins her). Emily Davis also honored (chapel; violets). Eleanor snaps at Bess: "footless little story." Jean's toasts "My Story and How I Wrote It" dropped.

## Ch IX THE COMPLICATIONS OF LIFE
- Basket-ball practice. Helen plays; Theresa (T. Reed).
- Lucy Merrifield (class president) appoints Betty to Students' Commission substitute for Christy Mason (mother ill). Dorothy King president of class and commission; Marion Lawrence junior rep.
- Miss Ferris tea: "What you did for Miss Watson was Students' Commission work."
- Mary's "hair-raising" for her mother Mrs. Brooks (ghost stories). Marion Lawrence and Frances West's letter on zoology bulletin board (dated Feb. 2 from "The Quiver," Fulton St., NY, Richard Blake).

## Ch X IN THE "ARGUS" SANCTUM
- Dorothy King delivers letter; Frances West (editor-in-chief, poet, dreamy), Beatrice Egerton (exchange editor). Letter from Richard Blake ("Dear Madame"): December Argus tribute; asks explanation; "We go to press on the twentieth inst." Frances replies.
- Blake's second letter: Eleanor's story is copy of "The Quiver" November story "The Lost Hope"; wants public acknowledgment. Editors debate; decide to ask Eleanor privately? Dorothy realizes she pressured Eleanor. Eleanor's story also copies from "The Quiver."

## Ch XI A PROBLEM IN ETHICS
- Dorothy ill (infirmary two weeks); asks Betty to go to New York to see Blake (Frances, Beatrice not suitable). Betty accepts after Eleanor's visit.
- Betty compares November Quiver date to barge ride. Madeline reveals she read "The Quiver" last fall (father sends it to her). Madeline: "Give him the benefit of the doubt."

## Ch XII A BRIEF FOR THE DEFENSE
- Betty writes Dorothy: "I am the one to go." Eleanor visits Betty, apologizes; says Jim coming Friday.
- Jim Watson visits (Judge's sons; Jim rooms? He's at Cornell). Jim walks with Betty to river; says Eleanor never wrote about story/club. Jim leaves Tuesday. Betty leaves Wednesday for NY.

## Ch XIII VICTORY OR DEFEAT
- Train delayed by blizzard; Betty stranded; Davidson Hotel with a gray-haired matron. Next day Blake's office (young, cynical; "Let us make a fair start"). Blake was pretending to be an assistant; reveals himself. Betty's argument; Blake: Shakespeare borrowed plots. Blake to lecture at Dramatic Club; coming to Harding.
- Betty home at 11:30pm; snowballs Belden windows; Madeline lets her in.

## Ch XIV A DISTINGUISHED GUEST
- Katherine invites Betty to "The Hand of Fate." Betty goes to Blake's lecture "The Tendencies of the Modern Drama." Blake and Madeline known (Paris crowd; calls him Dick). Miss Ferris dinner with Blake; Eleanor at his end. Blake asks Eleanor about honor code. Eleanor hears people; "Editor of The Quiver, Miss Watson."
- Eleanor writes new story (Jim's western experience).

## Ch XV DISAPPOINTMENTS
- Basket-ball game. Eleanor's song rejected; Helen's song chosen (T. Reed, "St. Louis" tune). Eleanor's story returned by Miss Raymond. Beatrice hints at Eleanor's secret to Jean; Betty interrupts. Helen wins praise. Christy back. Betty's idea: Miss Ferris.

## Ch XVI DORA CARLSON'S "SUGARING-OFF"
- Dora invites Eleanor to sugaring-off at Mrs. Bryant's kitchen (50 Market St.). Attendees: Betty, Beatrice, Nettie Dwight, two cousins. Fortunes from "Farmer's Friendly Counsellor"; Eleanor reads a compliment written by Dora that Beatrice mocks as irony; Eleanor's trust damaged.

## Ch XVII A MAY-DAY RESOLUTION
- May-day little girls party under apple trees. Miss Ferris picks Betty youngest. Eleanor refuses to join; walks with Miss Ferris to Paradise (woods). Eleanor confesses. Miss Ferris advises: resign from Dramatic Club and to not explain. Eleanor agrees to consider; Betty, Madeline, Mary find them.

## Ch XVIII TRIUMPHS AND TROUBLES
- Betty elected to Dramatic Club (eight pins). Helen's dress/tucks. Eleanor resigns (note Saturday night). Eleanor and Betty talk; Eleanor thanks her. Club accepts resignation for one year. Bob returns basket-ball song.

## Ch XIX GOOD-BYES
- Eleanor gives up her corner room to give Dora a cheaper room on Main Street. Betty and Helen decide to room together (T. Reed moves in). Betty becomes Dorothy King's successor (as president-ish). Roberta moves to Belden. Final talk with the girl from Bohemia: "So here's to junior year!" THE END.
